panels.description: Split of system.cpu.percent, which was the only CPU series plotted. iowait distinguishes CPU-bound from disk-bound.
panels.title: CPU Detail

panels.description: interrupts and soft_interrupts are scaled by 1000 so they are visible next to context switches, which are orders of magnitude larger.
panels.title: CPU Scheduling Activity

panels.description: Breakdown behind system.memory.used, which was the only memory series plotted.
panels.title: Memory Detail

panels.description: The whole swap family was unplotted. The live node currently runs at 100% swap used, which was invisible.
panels.title: Swap Usage

panels.description: Active swapping, as opposed to swap merely being allocated. Sustained sin/sout is what actually destroys latency.
panels.title: Swap Page Activity

panels.description: Values as emitted by systemMetricsDaemon.py. Busy time is the best available predictor of chainstate stalls; the board had only byte counters.
panels.title: Disk Saturation

panels.description: Host NIC throughput. Compare with the Bandwidth Usage dashboard, which measures the node's own P2P traffic; the difference is everything else on the box.
panels.title: Host Network Throughput

panels.description: Non-zero means the kernel is discarding packets, which surfaces as unexplained peer churn.
panels.title: Host Network Errors & Drops

panels.description: Resident set size of the node process, distinct from the host-level memory gauges.
panels.title: Node Process Footprint

panels.description: Approaching the ulimit is a hard failure waiting to happen.
panels.title: Open File Descriptors

panels.description: RPC threadpool pressure. Any queueDepthRejected means requests were refused outright.
panels.title: HTTP Work Queue

panels.description: A drop to zero is an unrecorded restart, which otherwise silently invalidates every cumulative counter.
panels.title: System Uptime
